span.label: A CONCEPT WHOSE OWN VOCABULARY IS THE EXAMPLE - information bias, itself `otherwise known as misclassification`, whose two main subtypes carry four names each in a single sentence apiece, with the alternatives listed and never distinguished

span.label: which forms of information bias arise in observational and experimental medical research, how each is recognised, and what can be done about it at design, measurement and analysis

span.label: a short taxonomy of information bias - self-reporting bias (social desirability, recall), measurement error bias, confirmation bias - each with its named alternatives, its typical study design, and an adjustment or prevention strategy

span.label: **ONE ERROR, FOUR NAMES, IN ONE SENTENCE**: `Quotation withheld` **Four names offered as interchangeable, with no test given for telling them apart** - and one of them, `measurement bias`, names the consequence while the others name the cause
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND AGAIN FOR THE THIRD FORM**: `Quotation withheld` And the paper's subject itself: `INFORMATION BIAS, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS MISCLASSIFICATION`. **Three concepts, four, four and two names, in one short review** - the corpus holds papers that count 138 definitions of a term; this is the same phenomenon at the scale of a synonym list, and it is not remarked on
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE TOP-LEVEL DEFINITION IS A GENUS AND A DIFFERENTIA: `Quotation withheld In health studies, bias can arise from TWO DIFFERENT SOURCES; the approach adopted for SELECTING SUBJECTS ... or the approach adopted for COLLECTING OR MEASURING DATA ... termed as SELECTION BIAS and INFORMATION BIAS.` **The partition is by WHERE THE ERROR ENTERS, not by what it does to the estimate** - which is why the same arithmetic consequence can belong to either
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND A DISTINCTION THE FIELD IS EXPLICITLY WARNED NOT TO COLLAPSE**: `Quotation withheld` The warning exists because the two are routinely conflated, and **the cost of conflating them is that the standard toolbox appears to cover both and covers one**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A TERM DEFINED BY WHAT IT IGNORES: `An analysis that IGNORES THE EFFECT OF MEASUREMENT ERROR on the results CAN BE REFERRED TO AS A NAIVE ANALYSIS.` Its consequences are given as `INCONSISTENT (OR BIASED) AND/OR INEFFICIENT ESTIMATORS of regression parameters`. **A name for the default practice**, which is the rhetorical move that makes an omission visible
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE MECHANISM OF RECALL BIAS IS SPELLED OUT AS A CHAIN: `in a case-control study, Quotation withheld As such, true exposure might be UNDERREPORTED IN HEALTHY CONTROLS AND OVERREPORTED IN THE CASES. THE SIZE OF THE DIFFERENCE ... WILL CONSEQUENTLY BE INFLATED, and, in turn, THE OBSERVED ODDS RATIO WOULD ALSO INCREASE.` **The bias has a direction, and the direction is predictable from the design** - which is what makes it adjustable at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE FIX FOR SELF-REPORTING IS VALIDATION AGAINST SOMETHING ELSE: `INTERNAL VALIDATION` compares responses `with other data collection methods, such as laboratory measurements`; `EXTERNAL VALIDATION` uses `medical record checks or reports from family or friends`. **The instrument is checked against a second instrument, never against the truth** - and the paper then says the laboratory measurements are themselves `often subject to measurement errors`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE VALIDATION HAS ITS OWN SAMPLING PROBLEM: `It is important to have A RANDOM SELECTION OF INDIVIDUALS so that results from the validation CAN BE GENERALIZED to any group of participants. WHEN THE SAMPLING APPROACH IS NOT RANDOM AND SUBJECTIVE, THE RESULTS FROM THE VALIDATION STUDY CAN ONLY APPLY TO THE SAME GROUP OF INDIVIDUALS.` **A correction factor inherits the scope of the study that produced it** - polman2011's MAGNIMS refusal, in a different discipline
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A WHOLE DESIGN IS DEMOTED ON THE STRENGTH OF ONE BIAS: `bias often accompanies results from case-control studies. Hence, CASE-CONTROL STUDIES CAN BE CONDUCTED IN ORDER TO GENERATE A RESEARCH HYPOTHESIS, BUT NOT TO EVALUATE PROGNOSES OR TREATMENT EFFECTS.` **A study design assigned a permitted use** - the same move donnelly2019 makes about a definition, here made about a method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE ONE FIELD THAT DOES ADJUST FOR MEASUREMENT ERROR IS NAMED: `Quotation withheld` **Where a number has to survive cross-examination, its error is modelled** - the practice follows the consequence, not the methodology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE AGREEMENT BETWEEN SELF-REPORT AND RECORDS IS DISEASE-SPECIFIC: `a HIGH AGREEMENT was found between self-reported questionnaires and medical record diagnoses of diseases such as DIABETES, HYPERTENSION, MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION, AND STROKE BUT NOT FOR HEART FAILURE.` **The instrument is not uniformly valid across the things it measures**, which is exactly what prigerson2009's differential item functioning analysis tests for and deletes
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE FOUR NAMES ARE LISTED AND NEVER SEPARATED.** `measurement error, instrumental error, measurement imprecision, or measurement bias` are offered as one thing; `confirmatory, ascertainment, or observer bias` likewise. Some of these are not synonyms in ordinary use - *instrumental* error is a subclass of measurement error, and *observer* bias is usually distinguished from *confirmation* bias by who holds the belief. **A review of error that hands the reader an unsorted synonym list is reproducing the problem it describes**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE ADVICE IS ADMITTED TO BE HARD TO FOLLOW: `Bias is often NOT ACCOUNTED FOR IN PRACTICE. Even though a number of adjustment and prevention methods ... are available, APPLYING THEM CAN BE RATHER CHALLENGING DUE TO LIMITED TIME AND RESOURCES. For example, MEASUREMENT ERROR BIAS PROPERTIES MIGHT BE DIFFICULT TO DETECT, particularly if there is A LACK OF INFORMATION ABOUT THE MEASURING INSTRUMENT.` The adjustment methods all require knowing the error distribution, and the error distribution requires a validation study that is `expensive`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE VALIDATION CHAIN BOTTOMS OUT ON ANOTHER MEASUREMENT: laboratory measurements are the recommended standard for validating self-report, and they are `OFTEN SUBJECT TO MEASUREMENT ERRORS` - `in a validation study to estimate sodium intake using a 24-hour urinary excretion method, THE ESTIMATED SODIUM INTAKE TENDED TO BE LOWER THAN THE TRUE AMOUNT`. **There is no step in the chain that touches the true value**, and the paper says so about its own recommended remedy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND CONFIRMATION BIAS IS THE ONE WITH NO ADJUSTMENT METHOD AT ALL: the remedies offered are independent checks, blinding, and `SPECIFIC EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS`, and the conclusion is `it is important to ACCEPT THAT BIAS IS A PART OF INVESTIGATIONS. QUANTIFYING THIS INEVITABLE BIAS and its potential sources MUST BE PART OF WELL-DEVELOPED CONCLUSIONS.` **The paper's title promises adjustment methods; for the third of its three biases there are none**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `bias` - `any systematic error in the design, conduct, or analysis of a study`; split by WHERE it enters into `selection bias` and `information bias`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `information bias` - `OTHERWISE KNOWN AS MISCLASSIFICATION`; error originating in `the approach that is utilized to obtain or confirm study measurements`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `measurement error` = `instrumental error` = `measurement imprecision` = `measurement bias` - four names presented as interchangeable in one sentence, with no criterion for choosing between them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `confirmation bias` - `OTHERWISE KNOWN AS CONFIRMATORY, ASCERTAINMENT, OR OBSERVER BIAS`: `a decision is made according to the subject's preconceptions, beliefs, or preferences`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `naive analysis` - `an analysis that IGNORES THE EFFECT OF MEASUREMENT ERROR on the results`. A name given to the default practice so that it can be argued against
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `systematic` vs `random` error - systematic deviations are `either consistently higher or lower than the true values`; random ones are `not consistent`, follow a distribution, and are called `multiplicative or non-gaussian` when proportional to the measurement
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → the existing bias literature, which the paper says has discussed types of bias while `the problem of bias is still frequently ignored in practice`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the naive analysis - the standard practice of ignoring measurement error, which yields `inconsistent (or biased) and/or inefficient estimators`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the use of case-control studies for anything beyond hypothesis generation, given that `bias often accompanies results from case-control studies`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → forensic toxicology, named as the one field with `the most theoretical understanding of measurement bias`, from which medical research is asked to learn
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: measurement error —same-as→ measurement bias
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9 — `Quotation withheld` **Four names, and they are not obviously synonyms**: instrumental error names a source, imprecision names a property of the instrument, and measurement bias names what the error does to the estimate. Tagged as the paper states it, and the un-sorted list is recorded as a limitation
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: confirmation bias —same-as→ observer bias
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9 — `Quotation withheld` **The second four-name list in one review.** In ordinary use `observer bias` is the observer's expectation affecting a measurement and `confirmation bias` is a search strategy over evidence; here they are one entry
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Bias —operationalised-as→ any systematic error in the design, conduct, or analysis of a study
span.term: any systematic error in the design, conduct, or analysis of a study
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld` **Systematic is doing all the work** - the definition excludes random error by construction, and the paper then spends its longest section on random measurement error, which is systematic in its effect on an estimate
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: selection bias —distinct-from→ information bias
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld` **A clean two-way split with a stated criterion**, which is more than most of the taxonomies in this corpus manage
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: random sampling —distinct-from→ measurement error variability
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld` **The warning is printed because the conflation is common, and the cost is specific**: the confidence interval looks complete and covers one of two error sources
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: An analysis that ignores the effect of measurement error on the results —same-as→ a naïve analysis
span.term: An analysis that ignores the effect of measurement error on the results
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9 — `An analysis that IGNORES THE EFFECT OF MEASUREMENT ERROR on the results CAN BE REFERRED TO AS A NAIVE ANALYSIS.` **Naming the default is how an omission becomes visible.** Compare carroll2007's `thinness` for missing fidelity data: both fields coined a word for a thing that is not there
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: cases —contrasted-with→ healthy controls
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `in a case-control study, Quotation withheld As such, true exposure might be UNDERREPORTED IN HEALTHY CONTROLS AND OVERREPORTED IN THE CASES.` **The bias is not noise; it has a sign that follows from the design**, which is why the paper can say what it does to the odds ratio
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The size of the difference between the observed rates of exposure to risk factors in cases and controls —causes→ the observed odds ratio

span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld` **A named error class traced all the way to the published statistic** - three steps, each stated, which is what makes recall bias adjustable rather than merely deplorable
